Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 57, verse 1:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir of Surat al-Hadid

It is Meccan according to al-Kalbi and a group of scholars. Some of them said: it is Medinan. It is related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr that he said: the Greatest Name of Allah is in the six verses at the beginning of Surat al-Hadid. It is also related from Abu al-Tayyah that he said: whoever wishes to know how the Compeller (al-Jabbar) described Himself, let him recite the six verses at the beginning of Surat al-Hadid. And Allah knows best.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Allah﴾. That is: prays and worships (sallā wa-ta'abbada). It is said: He is declared free of imperfection and sanctified (nazzaha wa-qaddasa). Some of them mentioned that the glorification of inanimate things is the trace of the Maker's workmanship in them. The more correct view is that it is literal glorification, and this is the view of the People of the Sunnah, because if the intended meaning were the trace of workmanship, then His saying ﴿but you do not understand their glorification﴾ would have no meaning, since the trace of workmanship is known and understood by everyone.

And His saying, ﴿and He is the Almighty, the All-Wise﴾: that is, the Victorious (al-Ghalib), the All-Wise in His command.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 57, verse 2:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth; He gives life and causes death﴾. That is: to Him belongs the dominion in the heavens and the earth, giving life and causing death. Al-Zajjaj said: He gives life from the dead drop (nutfah), and He causes death to the living person.

And the words of the Exalted: ﴿And He is over all things Competent﴾. That is: Capable (qadir).

The commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 57, verse 3:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿He is the First and the Last﴾ means: the First before everything, and the Last after everything. It was also said: the First, who has no beginning, and the Last, who has no end; and this is in the meaning of "the First." It was also said: the First without a beginning, and the Last without an end.

And His saying: ﴿and the Outward and the Inward﴾ means: the Outward by the proofs and signs, and the Inward because He is not seen by the eyes and is not perceived by the senses. It was also said: the Outward is the Dominant (al-Ghalib), and this is related from Ibn 'Abbas. And the Inward is the One who is veiled from His creation. (And it is related) from some of them: the One who knows what is apparent and what is hidden.

And His saying: ﴿And He is Knowing of everything﴾ means: Knowing (ʿAlim).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 57, verse 4:

The words of His, exalted is He, ﴿He it is who created the heavens and the earth in six days﴾. In the exegesis it is said that each day is a thousand years. It was also said that the names of the days are: abjad (abjad), hawwaz (hawwaz), huttı (ḥuṭṭī), kalaman (kalaman), sa'faṣ (saʿfaṣ), qarashat (qarashat).

The words of His, exalted is He: ﴿Then He istawa (istawā) over the Throne﴾. This has already been explained. It is related from Wahb ibn Munabbih that he said: the Throne was created from His light. It is related from some of them: it is a red ruby. The Throne was named "'arsh" (throne) because of its elevation.

His words: ﴿He knows what enters into the earth﴾, that is: what enters into it of rain, seed, and dead things.

His words: ﴿and what comes out of it﴾, that is: what enters into it of rain, seed, and dead things.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿and what comes out of it﴾, that is: of plants, trees, and the like.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿and what descends from the sky﴾, that is: of rain, provision, and angels.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿and what ascends into it﴾, that is: of angels and the deeds of the children of Adam.

His words: ﴿And He is with you wherever you are﴾, that is: by His knowledge and His power. This was mentioned by Ibn ʿAbbas and others. Al-Hasan said: "He is with you without how (bi-la kayf)."

His words: ﴿wherever you are﴾, that is: wherever you may be.

His words: ﴿And Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾, that is: Knowing (khabir).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 57, verse 5:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and to Allah all matters are returned﴾, meaning: all matters are brought back (to Him).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 57, verse 6:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He causes the night to enter into the day﴾, meaning: He diminishes from the night and increases in the day.

And His saying: ﴿and He causes the day to enter into the night﴾, meaning: He diminishes from the day and increases in the night.

And His saying: ﴿and He is Knower of what is within the breasts﴾, meaning: of what is in them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 57, verse 7:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Believe in God and His Messenger, and spend from that which He has made you inheritors of﴾. That is: spend from the wealth in which you were made successors (khalaf) to those before you. It was also said: "made you inheritors of it" means: granted you long life (mu'ammarin) with provision.

And His saying: ﴿So those of you who believe and spend, for them is a great reward﴾. That is: a great (ʿaẓīm) one.

"His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And what is [wrong] with you that you do not believe in Allah, while the Messenger invites you to believe in your Lord, and He has already taken your covenant, if you are [truly] believers?﴾ That is: the covenant from you. ﴿If you are believers﴾ That is: affirmers of the truth."

The Almighty's saying: ﴿He it is who sends down upon His servant clear signs, that He may bring you out from darkness into light﴾, meaning: from disbelief into faith.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Most Kind and Most Merciful to you﴾. We have already explained it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 57, verse 10:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And what is [the matter] with you that you do not spend in the way of Allah?﴾ Its meaning: that is, what benefit is there for you if you abandon spending in the way of Allah, while your wealth passes on to others? The meaning is a rebuke (inkar), as if He said: Why do you not spend your wealth so that you may reach Allah's reward through it, since it will not remain for you if you do not spend it?

And His saying: ﴿And to Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth﴾ is an indication of what we explained earlier.

﴿Those who spent and fought before the conquest are not equal [to the others]. They are greater in rank than those who spent and fought afterward. And to each Allah has promised the best.﴾

His saying: ﴿Not equal among you are those who spent and fought before the conquest﴾ means: those who spent and fought before the conquest of Makkah and those who spent and fought after the conquest of Makkah are not equal. They are not equal because the Companions of the Prophet suffered, before the conquest, hardship, difficulty, adversity and severity that they did not suffer after it. Al-Kalbi mentioned that the verse was revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him. It has also been narrated in some of the musnads from Ibn 'Umar that "the Prophet was sitting, and Abu Bakr al-Siddiq was with him, wearing a cloak that he had fastened at his chest. Jibril, peace be upon him, came and said to the Prophet: Allah, may He be exalted, says: Convey peace to Abu Bakr and tell him: Are you pleased with Me in your poverty, or angry? The Prophet said to Abu Bakr: This is Jibril, conveying to you the greeting of your Lord, and saying such-and-such. Abu Bakr wept and said: Rather, I am pleased with my Lord, rather, I am pleased with my Lord."

Al-Naqqash mentioned that the verse was revealed concerning 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, may Allah be pleased with him, who equipped the army of hardship (Jaysh al-'Usrah) and gave seven hundred and thirty camels and seventy horses, with their equipment.

In another narration: he brought five thousand dinars and poured them before the Prophet, and the Prophet, peace be upon him, began turning them over in his hand and saying: "Nothing that 'Uthman does after this will harm him."

His saying: ﴿They are greater in rank than those who spent and fought afterward﴾ — we have already explained the meaning of that.

His saying: ﴿And to each Allah has promised the best﴾ means: Paradise.

His saying: ﴿And Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾ means: Knowing. The meaning is that Allah, may He be exalted, promised Paradise to all the God-fearing, even though they differ in rank.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 57, verse 11:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Who is it that would lend to Allah a goodly loan﴾. ʿIkrimah said: When Allah the Exalted revealed this verse, Abu al-Dahdah gave in charity an orchard in which there were six hundred palm trees. In another narration: he gave in charity half of all his wealth, even his sandals; he gave one of them in charity. Then he came to his wife Umm al-Dahdah and said: "I have sold my Lord." She said: "May the sale be profitable." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "How many a palm tree hanging down for Abu al-Dahdah in Paradise, its roots of chrysolite and ruby."

And it is related from some of them that when this verse was revealed, the Jews came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "Is our Lord poor, that He asks us for loans?" So Allah the Exalted revealed His words: ﴿Allah has indeed heard the saying of those who said, "Indeed, Allah is poor and we are rich"﴾.

Al-Zajjaj said: The Arabs say of anyone who does a good deed: "He has lent," (qad aqraḍa, "he has lent" in the sense of doing a good act). The poet said:

(And when you are repaid a loan, repay it; / Indeed, a young man is repaid, not the camels.)

So the meaning of the verse according to this is: Who is it that does a good deed, so that Allah rewards him for it? And it is general in application.

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿so He multiplies it for him﴾ are read with the fa' in both the nominative and the accusative. With the nominative (fa-yuḍā'ifahu), it is coordinated with His words "would lend" (yuqriḍu). With the accusative, it is in answer to the interrogative with fa' (the particle fa' introducing the answer to a question, "so that").

His words: ﴿and for him is a noble reward﴾, meaning: a goodly one.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 57, verse 12:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿On the Day you see the believing men and believing women, their light running before them and on their right hands⦆... 

Let me correct that and render the passage exactly as given.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿On the Day you see the believing men and the believing women, their light running before them⦆. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "On the Sirat (the bridge over Hell)." It is related from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: "The light of each person is according to the measure of his deeds. Among them is one whose light is like a great mountain, among them is one whose light is like a palm tree, and among them is one whose light is upon his big toe; it goes out at times and flares up at others." In some reports: "Their light is what lies between Sana'a and Aden," meaning in terms of extent. It is related from Ibn 'Abbas, in the narration of al-Dahhak, that he said: "The Sirat is finer than a hair and sharper than a blade (al-shafra), and the believers pass over it with their light before them: some are like lightning, some like the wind, some like a bird, and some like the galloping of a horse."

The words of the Exalted: ﴿and on their right hands⦆, meaning: the light is on their right hands.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Good news for you today⦆, meaning: your glad tidings today ﴿are gardens beneath which rivers flow⦄.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Abiding therein; that is the supreme triumph⦆, meaning: the great salvation.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 57, verse 13:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿On the Day when the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women will say to those who believed, "Wait for us (unzurūnā)"﴾. It is from al-intiẓār (waiting, delaying). The most well-known of the two readings is the first, and its meaning is "Wait for us." As for the reading with an alif pronounced with a fatḥah (anẓirūnā), its meaning is "Be patient with us."

The poet said:

(Abā Hind, do not hasten against us... and give us respite, we will inform you with certainty.)

His saying: ﴿that we may acquire some of your light﴾. In the reports: people will be gathered while the hypocrites are mixed among the believers. Then God, Exalted is He, sends forth a light for the believers, and they walk in their light. The hypocrites follow them and say, "Wait for us, that we may acquire some of your light," for they had remained in darkness. In another report: people will be gathered, and a matter from the matters of God will overtake them, so the faces of the believers will become bright and the faces of the disbelievers will become dark. Then another matter will overtake them, and the light will be divided among the believers according to the measure of their deeds, while the disbelievers and the hypocrites remain in darkness, and they say to the believers, "Wait for us, that we may acquire some of your light."

His saying: ﴿naqtabis﴾ means: we take some of your light.

His saying: ﴿It will be said: "Return behind you"﴾ means: to the place where the light was distributed.

His saying: ﴿then seek light﴾ means: seek light there. They return but find nothing. Some of them said its meaning is: "Return to the world and seek the light through righteous deeds." This is said as reproach and rebuke, but it is a strange opinion, and the well-known one is the first.

His saying: ﴿So a wall will be struck between them, having a gate﴾. In the exegesis: when they return to that place and do not find the light, they go back to follow the light of the believers, and a punishment from the punishments of God overtakes them, and a wall is set between them and the believers. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿So a wall will be struck between them, having a gate﴾. It is also said: it is the al-A'rāf (the heights) mentioned in Surah al-A'rāf. It is reported from ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ that the wall is the eastern wall of the mosque of Bayt al-Maqdis, so the part adjoining the mosque is the one of which He said: ﴿Within it is mercy﴾, and the part adjoining the valley of Jahannam is the one of which He said: ﴿and without it is punishment﴾. There is a valley called the Valley of Jahannam, and it is well known.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 57, verse 14:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They will call out to them, "Were we not with you?"﴾ That is, the hypocrites will call out to the believers: "Were we not with you?" Its meaning: "Were we not with you in your prayer, your fasting, your mosques, and the like?"

And His saying: ﴿They will say, "Yes"﴾ That is: "Yes, you were with us outwardly."

And His saying: ﴿But you led yourselves into temptation﴾ That is: you employed yourselves in temptation (fitnah). It is said: "You led yourselves into temptation" means: you followed sins and desires.

And His saying: ﴿And you waited⁠—﴾ That is: you waited for the Prophet and the believers to be struck by the turns of fate (dawa'ir al-dahr). It is also said: "You waited" regarding repentance, meaning: you postponed it.

And His saying: ﴿And you doubted⁠—﴾ That is: you were in doubt about the religion.

And His saying: ﴿And false hopes deceived you⁠—﴾ That is: your wishful thinking that Muhammad would perish and his affair would be nullified.

And His saying: ﴿Until the command of Allah came⁠—﴾ That is: the command of Allah to grant victory to His Prophet and the believers. It is also said: the Fire.

And His saying: ﴿And the Deceiver deceived you concerning Allah⁠—﴾ That is: Satan. He was named "the Deceiver" (al-ghurur) because people deceive one another by inspiring them with falsehoods.

And it is narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr that he said: al-ghurur (deception) is that you commit sin and yet wish for Allah's forgiveness.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 57, verse 15:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿So today no ransom will be taken from you﴾. In the recitation of Ubayy ibn Ka'b, it is "jizyah" (poll-tax). The meaning of "fidyah" (ransom) is what a person ransoms his own self with from the punishment.

And His words: ﴿Nor from those who disbelieved. Your refuge is the Fire﴾, meaning: your station is the Fire.

And His words: ﴿It is your master﴾, meaning: the Fire is more fitting for you.

And His words: ﴿And wretched is the destination﴾, meaning: wretched is the place of return, the Fire.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 57, verse 16:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Has the time not come for those who believe⦆ mean: Has the time not drawn near (yaḥin), from al-ḥīn, which is the time.

It is said: āna yaʾīnu and ḥāna yaḥīnu carry the same meaning.

And His words: ﴿that their hearts should humble themselves to the remembrance of Allah﴾ mean: that they should soften and become tender.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: in the verse there is an exhortation to a group of the believers to be tender-hearted at the time of remembrance. And from Ibn Masʿud, who said: The period between the conversion of that people and the time when Allah rebuked them for abandoning humility and tenderness was only four years. And from Muqatil: the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) engaged in some levity concerning a matter of narration, so Allah the Exalted revealed this verse. And from some of them: the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) were afflicted with boredom, so they said: "Narrate to us, O Messenger of Allah," and Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿We relate to you the best of stories﴾. Then they were afflicted with boredom again, and Allah revealed: ﴿Allah has sent down the best of discourse﴾. Then they were afflicted with boredom again, and Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Has the time not come for those who believe that their hearts should humble themselves to the remembrance of Allah﴾.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: His words ﴿Has the time not come for those who believe﴾ refer to the believers among the People of the Book, urging them to believe in the Messenger. And from some of them: it refers to the hypocrites, who believed with their tongues but did not believe with their hearts. ﴿And what has been revealed of the truth﴾, [i.e.] the Qur'an.

And His words: ﴿And let them not be like those who were given the Scripture before⦆ mean: the Jews and the Christians.

And His words: ﴿so the term grew long for them⦆ mean: the duration, and it is said: the appointed term. And from Ibn Masʿud that he said: Do not ask the People of the Book about anything, for the term has grown long for them and their hearts have hardened; rather, what the Qur'an commands you, follow it, and what it forbids you, refrain from it.

And His words: ﴿and their hearts hardened⦆ mean: they dried up.

And His words: ﴿and many of them are defiant⦆ mean: they have departed from obedience to Allah. It is said: it refers to their innovating monasticism.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 57, verse 17:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Know that Allah gives life to the earth after its death﴾. It is reported in a report from Abu Razin al-Uqayli that he said: "O Messenger of Allah, how does Allah give life to the dead?" He (ﷺ) said: "Have you seen a land barren, and then you saw it green?" He said: "Yes." He said: "It is like that."

And it is reported from Salih al-Muzani that he said: He gives life to the hearts by softening them after their hardness. This is what is meant by the verse.

His saying: ﴿We have certainly made the signs clear to you, that you may understand﴾ — its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 57, verse 18:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who give charity, men and women, and lend to Allah a good loan﴾. It was recited with the ṣād doubled (muṣaddiqīn, muṣaddiqāt) and with the ṣād light (muṣṣaddiqīn, muṣṣaddiqāt). On the light ṣād, it means "the believers" (al-mu'minīn); on the doubled ṣād, it means "those who give charity" (al-mutaṣaddiqīn).

As for His saying: ﴿and lend to Allah a good loan﴾, it has been said: charity does not become "a good loan" until several qualities are gathered in it. The first of them: that it be from what is lawful; that he gives it with a good disposition of soul; that he does not follow it with reproach or harm; that he intends the good (al-jayyid) of his wealth, not the wicked (al-khabīth) and the inferior (al-radī'); that he gives it seeking the Face of Allah, not showing off to people; that he brings out the most beloved of his wealth to Allah, may He be exalted; that he gives charity while he is healthy, hoping to live and fearing poverty; that he does not consider what he has done to be great but regards it as small; and that he gives in abundance.

As for His saying: ﴿He will multiply it for them, and theirs will be a generous reward﴾, meaning: abundant and good.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 57, verse 19:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who believe in God and His messengers, those are the truthful (al-siddiqun)﴾. The siddiq is one who is greatly truthful, like al-sukayt, who is greatly silent.

It is related from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "All of you are siddiqs and martyrs." It was said to him: "How so, O Abu Hurayrah?" He recited his saying in this verse. The scholars differed concerning His saying: ﴿and the martyrs﴾. One opinion is that they are the well-known martyrs, those who were martyred in the way of God.

The second opinion is that they are the prophets; this was mentioned by al-Farra'.

The third opinion is that they are all the believers. According to this, al-shuhada' (the martyrs) is conjoined to His saying: ﴿those are the truthful﴾. According to the first two opinions, the pause and the sentence are complete at His saying: ﴿those are the truthful﴾, and His saying: ﴿and the martyrs, with their Lord﴾ is the beginning of a new statement. In His saying: ﴿with their Lord﴾ there is an indication of their station and rank with God.

His saying: ﴿For them is their reward and their light﴾, meaning: their recompense and their illumination.

His saying: ﴿And those who disbelieve and deny Our signs, those are the companions of the Blazing Fire (al-jahim)﴾ — its meaning is known; al-jahim is the greatest part of the Fire.

The commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 57, verse 20:

And His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Know that the life of this world is but play and amusement, adornment and boasting among you﴾. That is: it is that with which one plays, is amused, and adorns oneself. What is meant by it is: everything that is desired other than Allah, or everything that distracts from the religion. It is said: "Play and amusement" means eating and drinking. It is also said: "Play" refers to children, and "amusement" refers to women.

And His saying: ﴿boasting among you﴾, that is: boasting of some of you over others.

And His saying: ﴿and competing in multiplying wealth and children﴾, that is: vying with one another through the abundance of children and wealth. The difference between boasting (tafakhur) and competing in multiplying (takathur) is that boasting may occur between one who has children and wealth and one who has neither children nor wealth, whereas competing in multiplying occurs only between one who has children and wealth and another who has children and wealth.

It has been transmitted in some reports that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever seeks the world out of abstinence from asking others and to safeguard his child and dependants, will come on the Day of Resurrection with a face like the full moon on the night of the full moon. And whoever seeks it out of boasting, multiplying, and showing off to people, let him take his seat in the Fire," or words to this effect.

And His saying: ﴿like the rain whose vegetation pleases the disbelievers﴾, that is: the farmers, when it sprouts and becomes pleasing in the eyes of people.

And His saying: ﴿then it dries up and you see it turning yellow﴾, that is: it withers and dries out.

And His saying: ﴿turning yellow﴾, that is: yellow and dry.

And His saying: ﴿then it becomes debris﴾, that is: it breaks into pieces and crumbles. It has been said: it becomes a plant with no grain in it.

And His saying: ﴿and in the Hereafter there is severe punishment﴾, meaning: for those who prefer the world over the Hereafter.

And His saying: ﴿and forgiveness from Allah and approval﴾, meaning: for those who prefer the Hereafter over the world.

Qatadah said: The matter returns to these three phrases: ﴿and in the Hereafter there is severe punishment, and forgiveness from Allah and approval, and the life of this world is but the enjoyment of delusion﴾. As for "the enjoyment of delusion," we have already explained it earlier: it is everything that has no foundation, or everything that has no permanence.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 57, verse 21:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Race one another to forgiveness from your Lord﴾, meaning: hasten (sari'u). It is said: the racing is in faith. It is also said: in the first takbir (takbir al-ula, the opening takbir of prayer) and the first row (al-saff al-awwal). This is related from Rabah ibn 'Ubayda. And from Waki' ibn al-Jarrah, who said: "Whenever we saw a man neglecting the first takbir, we knew that he would not prosper."

And His words: ﴿and a garden whose width is like the width of the heaven and the earth﴾. What is meant by it is: join some of it to some, so that what they reach in total width is the width of the Garden. It is said: the racing is meant as racing toward repentance. It is also said: toward the Prophet (ﷺ).

And His words: ﴿whose width is like the width of the heaven and the earth﴾, that is, its vastness. The poet said:

(As if the lands of Allah, though they are wide, / over the fearful pursued one are a hunter's snare.)

And His words, may He be exalted: ﴿It is prepared for those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger﴾, that is, they affirmed Allah and affirmed His messengers to Him.

And His words: ﴿That is the bounty of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills, and Allah is the Possessor of great bounty﴾ — its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 57, verse 22:

The Exalted's saying: ﴿No calamity befalls the earth or your own selves⁠—﴾ "Calamity in the earth" is what befalls the earth of barrenness (jadb), drought (qahat), the destruction of fruits, and what is similar to that. "Calamity in the selves" is sickness (asqam), disease (amrad), and what resembles them.

His saying: ﴿except that it is in a Book⁠—﴾ It has been established that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When God created the Pen, He said to it: 'Write.' It said: 'And what shall I write?' He said: 'Write what will happen until the Day of Resurrection.'" The Book is the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz).

His saying: ﴿before We bring it into being⁠—﴾ That is: before We create it. The "writing" (al-kitabah) may refer to the inscriptions, and it may refer back to the calamity.

His saying: ﴿Indeed, that is easy for God.﴾ That is: easy (hayyin).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 57, verse 23:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿So that you do not grieve over what has escaped you﴾. Al-Asa (grief) is sorrow and regret.

And His words: ﴿nor exult over what He has given you﴾. That is: do not be insolent (tabattur) and do not be boastful (ta'shir). It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "There is no one who does not grieve, but what is meant by the verse is that we should give thanks at the time of blessing and be patient at the time of calamity." It is also related from some of them that its meaning is: he does not go beyond what Allah the Exalted has set as its limit, meaning: he does not lament at the time of calamity to the point of leaving off contentment, and he does not rejoice at the time of blessing to the point of departing from obedience to Allah, or of withholding its rights. Rather, when he knows that everything is by the decree and destiny of Allah, and that what has missed him would not have befallen him, and what has befallen him would not have missed him, then what has escaped him becomes easy for him, and he does not exult over what has reached him. It is related from 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz that he said: "When Allah withholds something from you, [what has escaped you], let that be a reason to abandon mentioning it."

And it is well known that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "To Allah belongs what He takes, and to Allah belongs what He gives."

And His words: ﴿Allah does not love every arrogant boaster﴾. That is: one who is proud and boastful of what he has been given.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 57, verse 24:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those who are niggardly and enjoin niggardliness upon the people﴾. The people of knowledge said: Bukhl (niggardliness) in its reality is withholding wealth from the right of God, exalted is He. Some of them said: If a person places it in other than its proper place, he is a miser even if he gives and gives much; and if he places it in its proper place, he is not a miser even if it is little. It is also reported from some of them that he said: Whoever pays the zakat of his wealth has been freed from niggardliness.

There is another view concerning the verse, mentioned by al-Suddi and others: that the verse refers to the Jews; their niggardliness is the concealment of the description of the Messenger, and their enjoining niggardliness upon the people is their enjoining concealment.

As for His saying: ﴿And whoever turns away, then indeed God is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy﴾, meaning: Self-Sufficient above the obedience of His creatures, Praiseworthy in His actions. It has also been said: Self-Sufficient above the charities of the creatures, Praiseworthy in His bounty upon them.

It is related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr that he said: "Those who are niggardly" means: they do not give charity; "and enjoin niggardliness upon the people" means: to abandon charity. The difference between the miser (bakhil) and the generous (sakhi) is that the generous is one who takes pleasure in giving, while the miser is one who takes pleasure in withholding. It has also been said: the miser is one who gives what he gives while his soul is not content, and the generous is one who gives what he gives with his soul content with it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 57, verse 25:

His words, exalted is He: ﴿We indeed sent Our messengers with clear proofs and sent down with them the Book﴾, meaning: the books.

And His words: ﴿and the Balance﴾. Qatadah said: it is justice. Al-Kalbi said: the Balance is the well-known instrument by which things are weighed, and its meaning is: We set up the balance. According to the first view, its meaning is: We commanded justice.

And His words: ﴿that mankind may uphold justice﴾, meaning: with justice in the weighing.

And His words: ﴿And We sent down iron, wherein is great might﴾. Regarding His words ﴿We sent down iron﴾ there are two views. The first: its meaning is "We created iron and brought it into being."

The second view: what is meant is literal sending down from the sky, and that when Allah, exalted is He, sent Adam down to the earth, He sent down with him the al-'alah (tongs), the two pincers, and the mi'qa'ah, which is the hammer. It was also said: He sent down with him the Black Stone, the staff of Moses made of myrtle from Paradise, and the iron we have mentioned.

And His words: ﴿wherein is great might﴾, meaning: it is a weapon and a shield. The weapon is fought with, and the shield is used for protection.

And His words: ﴿and benefits for mankind﴾ refers to what is made from iron tools, such as the axe, the adze, the saw, the awl, the needle and similar things.

And His words: ﴿that Allah may know who helps Him and His messengers unseen﴾. He mentioned this here because the help of Allah, exalted is He, and the help of His messengers, is by fighting, and fighting is with iron implements. He said ﴿unseen﴾ because all the acts of obedience that the servants perform, they perform in the unseen, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿those who believe in the unseen﴾.

And His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Strong, Mighty﴾: its meaning is apparent.

Almost verbatim: the Qur'anic quotation is in ﴿ ﴾ with plain translation inside.

Translation:

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And We certainly sent Noah and Abraham and placed in their offspring prophethood and the Scripture, so among them is one who is guided﴾, i.e., a Muslim. ﴿And many of them are defiantly disobedient﴾, i.e., disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 57, verse 27:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then We sent after them Our messengers﴾, i.e., We made [others] follow [them].

And His saying: ﴿And We sent after them Jesus, son of Mary, and gave him the Gospel﴾, i.e., We gave him the Gospel in its entirety.

And His saying: ﴿And We placed in the hearts of those who followed him compassion and mercy﴾. Ra'fah (compassion) is the intensest form of mercy. By these [people] is meant those who remained upon the religion of truth and did not alter or change it after Jesus, peace be upon him.

And His saying: ﴿But monasticism they invented﴾, i.e., they invented monasticism on their own initiative. Rahbaniyyah (monasticism) is what they invented of wandering through the deserts and wastelands (and the barren tracts). It was said: it is seclusion in homes and monasteries for worship. It has been narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "There is no monasticism in Islam." And in another narration he said: "The monasticism of my community is jihad in the way of Allah." In the reports it is mentioned that the cause of their invention of monasticism was that the kings after Jesus, peace be upon him, altered the religion of Jesus and killed the worshippers and the righteous among the Children of Israel when they called them to the truth. So the righteous among them said to one another, and they were the ones who remained: "Indeed, even if they kill us, it is not befitting for us to remain among them in silence." So some of them joined the deserts and wandered, and some of them built monasteries and secluded themselves in them for worship. Thus the origin of monasticism was for this reason.

And His saying: ﴿We did not prescribe it for them﴾, i.e., We did not make it obligatory upon them.

And His saying: ﴿except seeking the pleasure of Allah﴾. It is in the accusative as an object of an omitted verb; the omitted [phrase] is: they invented it only seeking the pleasure of Allah.

And His saying: ﴿but they did not observe it with its proper observance﴾, i.e., they did not uphold it as it should be upheld.

And His saying: ﴿So We gave those of them who believed their reward﴾, i.e., their recompense, and they are those who believed in Muhammad after having been ascetics.

And His saying: ﴿and many of them are defiantly disobedient﴾, i.e., those who remained upon disbelief.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 57, verse 28:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and believe in His Messenger; He will give you a double portion of His mercy﴾. That is: two shares. It was also said: two rewards from His mercy. In the tafsir (exegesis) it is related that the reason for the revelation of the verse was that when Allah, may He be exalted, revealed to them His saying: ﴿And when it is recited to them, they say, "We have believed in it; indeed, it is the truth from our Lord"﴾ up to His saying: ﴿Those will be given their reward twice﴾, the believers among the People of the Book boasted over the rest of the believers from the Companions, and they said: "You will be given your reward once, while we will be given it twice." So Allah, may He be exalted, revealed this verse as glad tidings to the rest of the believers. It has also been established from the Prophet, through the transmission of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, that he said, upon him be prayers and peace: "Three will be given their reward twice: a man who believed in the first Book and then believed in the second Book; a man who bought a slave-girl, disciplined her and perfected her discipline, then freed her and married her; and a slave who obeyed his Lord and gave sincere counsel to his master." It was also said: His saying, ﴿He will give you a double portion of His mercy﴾ refers to the reward of the secret (deed) and the reward of the open (deed). It was also said: the reward of fulfilling the right of Allah, may He be exalted, and fulfilling the rights of the servants.

And His saying: ﴿and will make for you a light by which you will walk﴾ is the light which we explained earlier, which will illuminate them upon the Path (al-sirat). It was also said: it is the light of Islam.

And His saying: ﴿by which you will walk﴾ means: you will follow the way of Islam by its light.

And His saying: ﴿and will forgive you; and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ is clear in meaning.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 57, verse 29:

The words of the Most High: ﴿That the People of the Scripture may know﴾ — "that" (li-allā) and "so that" (li-ka-yalā) have one meaning, and this is the explanation of the well-known reading. Al-Akhfash (al-Akhfash al-Awsat), al-Farra' and others said: the "lā" here is superfluous (ṣila), and it is like the saying of the poet:

(And I do not blame the fair ones that they do not bewitch...)

meaning: that they bewitch.

As for His words: ﴿that they have no power over anything of the bounty of Allah﴾, its meaning is: We gave what We gave of the double portion of mercy to the believers, so that the People of the Scripture would know that the conveying of the bounty of Allah is not in their hands, and the believers would know that the bounty is in the hand of Allah, He gives it to whom He wills. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿and that the bounty is in the hand of Allah; He gives it to whomever He wills﴾, i.e., He gives it to whomever He wills. It has also been said that the meaning of the verse is: so that the People of the Scripture would know that whoever does not believe in Muhammad (ﷺ) has no share of the bounty of Allah on the Day of Resurrection.

And His words: ﴿they have no power over anything of the bounty of Allah﴾, i.e., they do not reach anything of the bounty of Allah since they did not believe in Muhammad (ﷺ), while the bounty is in the hand of Allah, who conveys it to the believers in Muhammad (ﷺ) by His will. The bounty here is Paradise.

And His words: ﴿and Allah is the Possessor of great bounty﴾, i.e., He has great bounty, and He is able to convey great bounty — meaning: to whomever He wills of His servants. And Allah knows best what is correct.
